questions.q: Genu varum (bow legs) is the deformity in which the knees deviate:
questions.exp: Genu varum (bow knees/legs): knees away from the midline. (Book p166)

questions.q: Genu valgum (knock knees) is the deformity in which the knees deviate:
questions.exp: Genu valgum (knock knees): towards the midline. (Book p166)

questions.q: Windswept deformity is:
opts: One leg varus and the other valgus
questions.exp: Windswept deformity: one leg varus and the other valgus. (Book p166)

questions.q: Genu recurvatum (back knees) is characterized by:
opts: Excessive backward bending of the knee
questions.exp: Genu recurvatum (back knees): excessive backward bending. (Book p166)

questions.q: The m/c cause of B/L genu varum (bow legs) in children is:
questions.exp: B/L genu varum in children: rickets > idiopathic. (Book p166)

questions.q: The m/c cause of B/L genu valgum in children is:
questions.exp: B/L genu valgum in children: idiopathic > rickets. (Book p166)

questions.q: The m/c cause of windswept deformity in children is:
questions.exp: Windswept deformity in children: rickets. (Book p166)

questions.q: The m/c cause of B/L genu varum in adults is:
questions.exp: B/L genu varum in adults: osteoarthritis > rheumatoid arthritis. (Book p166)

questions.q: The m/c cause of B/L genu valgum in adults is:
questions.exp: B/L genu valgum in adults: rheumatoid arthritis > osteoarthritis. (Book p166)

questions.q: The m/c cause of windswept deformity in adults is:
questions.exp: Windswept deformity in adults: rheumatoid arthritis. (Book p166)

questions.q: Blount's disease (infantile tibia vara) is:
questions.exp: Blount's disease / infantile tibia vara: B/L idiopathic genu varum. (Book p166)

questions.q: The pathological defect in Blount's disease is the:
questions.exp: Blount's disease: proximal medial tibial physis defect. (Book p166)

questions.q: Besides the physis defect, the features of Blount's disease include:
opts: Internal rotation of tibia and genu recurvatum (hyperextension)
questions.exp: Blount's disease: internal rotation of tibia; genu recurvatum (hyperextension). (Book p166)

questions.q: The clinical sign of Blount's disease is:
questions.exp: Blount's disease: sign = Sifert Katz sign. (Book p166)

questions.q: The X-ray finding in Blount's disease is:
questions.exp: X-ray: metaphyseal beaking. (Book p166)

questions.q: The causes of (acquired) knee deformity include:
questions.exp: Causes of deformity: malunion; growth plate injury. (Book p167)

questions.q: Open wedge osteotomy corrects deformity by:
opts: Shortening the long side by removing bone
Lengthening the short side by filling extra bone
questions.exp: Open wedge osteotomy: lengthen the short side by filling extra bone. (Book p167)

questions.q: Closed wedge osteotomy corrects deformity by:
opts: Shortening the long side by removing bone
questions.exp: Closed wedge osteotomy: shorten the long side by removing bone. (Book p167)

questions.q: The action of the tibio-talar / ankle joint is:
questions.exp: Tibio-talar / ankle joint: ankle plantar / dorsiflexion. (Book p167)

questions.q: The action of the talocalcaneal / subtalar joint is:
questions.exp: Talocalcaneal / subtalar joint: inversion / eversion of foot. (Book p167)

questions.q: The talonavicular and calcaneocuboid (mid tarsal) joints perform:
questions.exp: Talonavicular and calcaneocuboid / mid tarsal joint: forefoot adduction / abduction. (Book p167)

questions.q: The medial longitudinal arch of the foot provides its concavity; when it is lost the condition is:
questions.exp: Medial longitudinal arch: provides concavity of the foot; lost: flat foot; exaggerated: cavus of foot. (Book p167)

questions.q: Ankle plantarflexion deformity at the ankle joint is called:
questions.exp: Ankle joint / tibio-talar joint: ankle plantarflexion -> equinus deformity. (Book p168)

questions.q: Ankle dorsiflexion deformity is called:
questions.exp: Ankle dorsiflexion -> calcaneus deformity. (Book p168)

questions.q: Inversion of the foot at the subtalar / talocalcaneal joint is a:
questions.exp: Subtalar / talocalcaneal joint: inversion of foot -> varus deformity. (Book p168)

questions.q: Eversion of the foot at the subtalar / talocalcaneal joint is a:
questions.exp: Eversion of foot -> valgus deformity. (Book p168)

questions.q: Talipes is defined as:
opts: Congenital deformity in which the foot is twisted
questions.exp: Terminology: talipes = congenital deformity in which the foot is twisted. (Book p168)

questions.q: Talipes cavus is:
questions.exp: Talipes cavus: high arched foot. (Book p168)

questions.q: Talipes equinus is:
questions.exp: Talipes equinus: plantarflexion. (Book p168)

questions.q: Talipes calcaneus is:
questions.exp: Talipes calcaneus: dorsiflexion. (Book p168)

questions.q: Talipes valgus is:
questions.exp: Talipes valgus: abduction and eversion. (Book p168)

questions.q: Talipes varus is:
questions.exp: Talipes varus: adduction and inversion. (Book p168)

questions.q: Congenital Talipes Equinus Varus (CTEV) is also known as:
opts: Club foot (appears like a golf club)
questions.exp: CTEV: aka club foot (appears like a golf club). (Book p168)

questions.q: CTEV is the m/c:
opts: Congenital abnormality of leg, ankle and foot
questions.exp: CTEV is the m/c congenital abnormality of leg, ankle and foot. (Book p168)

questions.q: In CTEV, the proportion of bilateral cases is:
questions.exp: Epidemiology: 50%: bilateral. (Book p168)

questions.q: The incidence of CTEV is:
questions.exp: Epidemiology: 1/1000 live births. (Book p168)

questions.q: CTEV is more common in:
questions.exp: Males > females. (Book p168)

questions.q: CTEV is associated with:
opts: 1st born child a/w fetal malpresentation like breech
questions.exp: Epidemiology: 1st born child a/w fetal malpresentation like breech. (Book p168)

questions.q: The m/c type of CTEV is:
opts: Congenital / primary CTEV, with idiopathic as the m/c cause
questions.exp: Etiology: 1. congenital / primary CTEV: m/c type; m/c cause: idiopathic. (Book p168)

questions.q: CTEV is seen in association with:
questions.exp: Etiology includes spina bifida. (Book p168)

questions.q: In arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, the pathogenesis of CTEV is:
questions.exp: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita: muscle fibrosis -> contracture -> deformity. (Book p168)

questions.q: The acquired causes of CTEV are:
questions.exp: Acquired causes: neuromuscular disorders (poliomyelitis). (Book p168)

questions.q: The pathoanatomy of CTEV begins with:
opts: Hypoplastic (small) talus -> talonavicular joint dislocation -> unstable foot -> pull by tendoachilles and tibialis posterior -> deformity
questions.exp: Pathoanatomy: hypoplastic talus (small) -> talonavicular joint dislocation -> unstable foot -> pull by tendoachilles and tibialis posterior -> deformity (foot appears pulled posteriorly and medially). (Book p169)

questions.q: In CTEV, as per the diagram:
opts: The talus is in equinus and varus, the calcaneus is inverted, the forefoot bones are in varus, and the ankle joint is in plantarflexion
questions.exp: Diagram: plantarflexion of ankle joint; talus in equinus and varus; inversion of calcaneus; forefoot bones in varus. (Book p169)

questions.q: In the primary deformities of CTEV, 'C' stands for Cavus, which is:
opts: Exaggeration of the medial longitudinal arch
questions.exp: Primary deformities: C: cavus - exaggeration of medial longitudinal arch. (Book p169)
